records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: arXiv preprint 2602.22359v1, submitted 26 February 2026; peer review not established
records.decision_reason: The study experimentally varies prompts in an LLM-assisted interpretive citation-context analysis, inductively codes 450 generated readings, and treats plurality and prompt sensitivity as methodological outcomes.

Research objective.value: Test whether GPT-5 can support thick, text-grounded interpretive citation-context analysis and quantify how scaffolding and framing alter the interpretations it foregrounds.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: interpretative citation-context analysis, close reading and inductive coding

Actual operationalized methodology.value: A two-stage GPT-5 pipeline first classifies one canonical citation and generates expectations, then receives citing/cited full texts and produces five hypotheses per run under a balanced 2x3 scaffold-by-nudge design; the sole author close-reads and inductively codes 450 hypotheses into 21 recurring moves and models condition effects.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid: deductive surface typology plus inductive coding of open-ended interpretations

Domain.value: sociology of science and interpretive citation-context analysis

Number of documents.value: one hard citation case using the complete citing and cited papers plus Gilbert's published interpretation

Prompting strategy.value: Prompt-chained surface and reconstruction stages; stage two crosses one-step versus four-step scaffolding with no, toward-case, or away-case nudges; full prompts are supplied.

Human role.value: The author designs prompts, selects the canonical case, samples stage-one outputs, close-reads/codes every hypothesis, judges plausibility and retains final interpretive authority.
Human role.anchor: human reader as curator and critic

Unit of analysis.value: hypothesis-justification pair about one citation context
Unit of analysis.anchor: each treated as a single interpretative unit

Generated outputs.value: 30 surface classifications, 90 reconstructions, 450 hypotheses/justifications, 21 inductive move codes and prompt-effect estimates

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Every hypothesis must justify itself with the supplied full texts; prompts and exemplar outputs are reproduced, but the article does not release a row-level source/coding ledger.

Number of runs or seeds.value: 30 stage-one runs; 15 randomly sampled seeds crossed with six prompt conditions for 90 stage-two runs; no seed value reported

Automatic metrics.value: frequencies, lexical repertoires, saturated 2x3 linear-probability models, average marginal effects and confidence intervals

Human-evaluation design.value: single-author close reading/coding with comparison to Gilbert's historical interpretation; no independent second coder

Principal results.value: Surface labels stayed supplementary (30/30; 19 perfunctory and 11 additional-information for G&W). Reconstruction generated 21 recurring moves; prompt design systematically but often modestly redistributed interpretations/lexicon, and no run fully recovered Gilbert's admonishment reading.

Efficiency or cost results.value: 5,034,263 input and 618,284 output tokens (518,080 reasoning); approximately US$6.24 total. Four-step runs used more output tokens than one-step (7,271 versus 6,469 per run, reported aggregate comparison).

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: No participant data; copyrighted scholarly full-text PDFs were sent to a proprietary API, with data-governance/licensing implications not discussed.

Author-reported limitations.value: Single canonical case, single analyst, one opaque proprietary model, high resource/LLM-literacy requirements, and no cross-model comparison.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: 450 hypotheses are nested within only 90 runs and one source case, so hypothesis-level linear models risk pseudo-replication; inductive code construction and plausibility judgments have no independent audit.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Material support for a prompt-fragility arm that treats interpretive multiplicity as signal, preregisters prompt factors, and evaluates source-grounded hypotheses rather than collapsing them to one answer.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: arXiv preprint 2607.21549v1, submitted 23 July 2026; peer review not established
records.decision_reason: The paper uses interdisciplinary open coding to build a sensitive-domain taxonomy and validates multiple LLM-assisted coding/judging stages against human reference labels at corpus scale.

Research objective.value: Characterize technology-facilitated-abuse help-seeking and compare the relevance, accuracy, actionability and safety of search, peer forums and conversational AI.
Research objective.anchor: large-scale evaluation of online support systems

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: iterative qualitative open coding plus expert manual evaluation

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Computer-science and social-work coders create an 11-category abuse taxonomy from Reddit posts; held-out-validated prompt classifiers scale labels and extract victim queries; multi-background coders create rubrics/reference labels for technical and trauma-informed response qualities; validated LLM classifiers/judges scale selected technical dimensions while social dimensions stay manual.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid: inductive taxonomy construction followed by deductive multilabel classification and rubric-based evaluation

Domain.value: technology-facilitated abuse, victim help-seeking, cybersecurity and trauma-informed support

Number of documents.value: 3,266 Reddit posts and 32,162 comments (2014-2024); Llama extracted 5,926 questions and 2,797 victim-authored TFA queries; 27,970 search URLs, 17,714 Reddit comments and 250 chatbot responses were evaluated

Number of participants.value: No recruited participants; two CS coders label 210 posts, two social-work coders label 398 targeted posts, and later validation tasks use two or three coders with CS/social-work expertise

Sensitive-data status.value: public but highly sensitive stalking/abuse narratives; local models, anonymization/paraphrase/redaction and partial artifact release used to reduce disclosure and retraumatization risks

Model family.value: GPT, Claude, Gemini, Llama, GPT-OSS, Gemma and specialist chatbots

Exact model/version.value: GPT-OSS 20B for 11 classifiers; Llama 3.3 and GPT-4 for query extraction; Llama 3.3/GPT-OSS 20B/Gemma3:12b judge ensemble; evaluated GPT-5, Claude Opus 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, HopeChat and Ruth

Prompting strategy.value: Few-shot per-category binary prompts with labelled examples and iterative refinement; separate query-extraction, victim-role/TFA, relevance and judge prompts; prompts disclosed in appendices/repository.

Human role.value: Interdisciplinary teams construct categories/rubrics, double-code samples, resolve disagreements, validate automated stages, and manually score all subtle social/trauma dimensions.

Unit of analysis.value: Reddit post/question, webpage-query pair, comment thread or chatbot question-answer pair depending on stage

Generated outputs.value: 11-category taxonomy, victim queries, multilabel abuse codes, platform responses and technical/social safety ratings

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Queries retain source-post association; rubrics/prompts/code and representative processed data are released, but complete sensitive data and full row-level outputs are withheld.
Evidence/provenance mechanism.anchor: representative sample rather than the complete dataset

Automatic metrics.value: accuracy, precision, recall, F1, semantic similarity, readability, Perspective-API toxicity, kappa, Krippendorff alpha and Gwet AC1

Human-evaluation design.value: Multiple held-out coder validations: misuse categories kappa .66-1.0/.73; query labels .62/.90; response relevance .62; technical accuracy .48-.88 depending source; three experts manually rate 250 chatbot pairs, with low alpha but higher AC1 for imbalanced social labels.
Human-evaluation design.anchor: Three coders independently annotated all responses

Principal results.value: Taxonomy classifiers generally achieved F1 above .85; Llama query filters achieved .86/.96 F1. Search/LLMs were more relevant/actionable than Reddit, but search exposed malicious destinations, over 20% of Reddit threads contained toxicity, and all chatbots had trauma-informed limitations.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Local processing prevented transmitting sensitive Reddit text; examples were anonymized/paraphrased/redacted; trauma-informed protocols involved social workers; only representative artifacts are released.

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors note one subreddit, historical deletions/coverage, platform sampling, classifier error, limited representative release and risks in generalizing simulated help-seeking to real victims.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: many sequential model filters can compound selection error; model names lack dated snapshots; some validation sets are very small and imbalanced, agreement is low on key social dimensions, and victims did not evaluate the advice themselves.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Shows how expert composition, disagreement metrics robust to imbalance, sensitive-data containment, failure propagation and manual retention of subtle dimensions should enter an end-to-end qualitative-coding benchmark.
Relevance to the proposed ARR project.anchor: current LLM evaluators may not reliably capture

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: arXiv preprint 2601.09905v1, submitted 14 January 2026; peer review not established
records.decision_reason: The study directly evaluates a human-guided secondary LLM critic for large-scale qualitative coding using gold labels, deployment audits and error-specific prompt refinement.

Research objective.value: Determine whether a targeted second LLM critique can reduce systematic false positives from a first-pass qualitative-code classifier without abandoning human-designed constructs.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: LLM-assisted qualitative coding with inductive error analysis and bounded human-in-the-loop adjudication

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Researchers adapt a human codebook of six project-evaluation justification codes, validate per-code GPT-4o prompts on 120 human-coded emails, label 3,149 emails, audit 60 predicted positives/code, induce two recurrent error types, build a positive-only critic prompt, and estimate prevalence-corrected stage-one/stage-two performance on an additional random sample.
Actual operationalized methodology.anchor: Our study proposes a two-stage annotation workflow

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid: deductive six-code application plus inductive model-error taxonomy

Domain.value: Apache Software Foundation project-incubation evaluation emails

Number of documents.value: 3,149 high-content emails; 120-email initial gold set; 360 audited predicted positives; 150 randomly sampled passages for prevalence-consistent pipeline estimates

Number of participants.value: human coder counts not fully reported; one author audited deployment positives

Sensitive-data status.value: public/open-source project email discussions; privacy treatment not reported

Exact model/version.value: gpt-4o-2024-08-06 at temperature 0 and top-p 1 for both stages

Prompting strategy.value: Six separate codebook-derived binary prompts elicit label plus text rationale; a second positive-only call receives passage, code definition and first rationale, applies sufficiency/error rules and returns structured JSON; two code-specific addenda target observed failures.
Prompting strategy.anchor: Our critic prompt has three layers

Human role.value: Researchers design/adapt codes, adjudicate the initial gold set, audit positives, induce error classes, tighten human rules and critic clauses, and retain authority to revise both model and gold labels.

Unit of analysis.value: email passage by binary qualitative code

Generated outputs.value: six binary labels with rationales, critic confirm/veto decisions, error taxonomy (misinterpretation and meta-discussion), and prevalence-corrected performance

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Stage-one text-tethered rationale is retained and reviewed with the original passage by human and critic; machine-readable JSON supports audit.
Evidence/provenance mechanism.anchor: reads the original passage and the first model's rationale

Number of runs or seeds.value: one temperature-zero stage-one call per message-code and one critic call for every predicted positive; no cross-run or cross-model stability test

Automatic metrics.value: false-positive rates, precision, recall, F1, Cohen kappa, positive rates and prevalence-corrected reconstructed confusion matrices

Human-evaluation design.value: Human-coded 120-email prompt-validation set; one-author audit of 360 predicted positives; separate random 150-passage prevalence sample; rationales used to find candidate spans but validity judged against text/code definitions.

Principal results.value: First-stage deployment false-positive rates ranged 8%-54% despite test F1 .74-1.00. Critique improved F1 by .04-.25; Mentor Engagement rose .55 to .79 and Technical/Market .52 to .69, largely by pruning misinterpretation/meta-discussion errors.

Efficiency or cost results.value: Critic operates only on stage-one positives (about 15% overall) and is described as compute-light; time/token/cost totals are not reported.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: No formal ethics/privacy discussion reported for the public email corpus.

Author-reported limitations.value: Positive-only critique cannot fix false negatives; performance/error taxonomy may not transfer across codes/corpora; evaluation and error analysis depend heavily on the human gold standard and targeted sampling.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: one author performs the key deployment audit and reads model rationales, creating anchoring risk; iterative tightening of prompts and human gold rules can overfit this corpus; same-model self-critique is not independent corroboration.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: High-impact benchmark design: separate prompt-development, deployment audit and prevalence sample; evaluate code-specific errors and negative-class coverage rather than relying on small balanced test F1.
Relevance to the proposed ARR project.anchor: Good test-set performance does not guarantee

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: arXiv preprint 2603.04413v2, submitted March 2026; peer review not established
records.decision_reason: The paper proposes and empirically applies a human-grounded qualitative metric to compare LLM and human thematic summaries across five corpus sizes and repeated runs.

Research objective.value: Develop an Inductive Conceptual Rating (ICR) for conceptual/meaning fidelity and test whether lexical similarity overstates the quality of LLM thematic summaries.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: Reflective thematic analysis and inductive content analysis

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Multiple researchers create three-theme RTA baselines for five nested/open-text work-perception datasets, separately induce concept categories from LLM outputs, score concept presence/omission/addition with an accuracy-like ICR, and compare two models over ten runs each with cosine similarity/BERTScore.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: inductive human RTA and inductive LLM-output content coding followed by deductive concept matching

Domain.value: open-ended survey responses about perceptions of work/work-life harmony

Number of documents.value: five datasets of 50, 100, 200, 400 and 800 responses (1,550 response instances; nesting/independence not specified)

Number of participants.value: number of human researchers not reported; multiple raters are stated

Sensitive-data status.value: personally identifying information removed; source data and consent/governance not otherwise reported

Exact model/version.value: Claude Sonnet 3.5 and Amazon Nova Pro; dated snapshots/API versions not reported

Prompting strategy.value: Dozens of zero-/few-shot/chain-of-thought prompts iteratively tuned per model; final prompts require exactly three named themes and 3-4 sentence JSON summaries; temperature 0, top-k .25, top-p .99.

Human role.value: Researchers conduct RTA, induce/correct concept categories, code human/model outputs, resolve ambiguity and define the reference interpretation.
Human role.anchor: researchers conducted a Reflective Thematic Analysis

Unit of analysis.value: source response for RTA; sentence/meaningful phrase and concept presence for output evaluation

Generated outputs.value: three themes/summary per dataset/model/run, RTA themes, ICA concepts and ICR/cosine/BERTScore results

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Concept-level human/LLM comparison tables and examples are provided, but complete response-to-theme traces and data are not reported.
Evidence/provenance mechanism.anchor: presence or absence of each concept was documented

Number of runs or seeds.value: ten runs per model-prompt-dataset; 50 outputs/model and 100 total; modal/most recurring output selected; seeds not reported
Number of runs or seeds.anchor: each prompt and model was run ten times

Automatic metrics.value: cosine similarity, BERTScore and ICR accuracy over concept true positives, false positives, false negatives and true negatives

Human-evaluation design.value: Multiple raters build baselines and code LLM outputs; appendix reports Cohen kappa .87 and Fleiss kappa .85 for RTA and Cohen kappa .81 for ICA, but coder count/assignment/blinding are not reported.

Principal results.value: Human ICR stayed .86-1.00; LLM ICR ranged .35-.76 despite high lexical metrics. At N=100 Sonnet cosine .89/F1 .91 but ICR .35; at N=800 Sonnet/Nova ICR improved to .65/.76 versus human .93.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: PII was removed; no ethics approval, consent, data source, access controls or model data-retention discussion is reported.

Author-reported limitations.value: One survey question/domain, situated rather than universal human ground truth, only two models with tailored prompts, and binary concept presence ignores degrees, relations and emphasis.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: dataset nesting/independence and coder numbers are unclear; model-specific prompts were tuned on output alignment with the objectives; selecting the modal run and defining ICR concepts from analyst judgment may inflate apparent validity; ICR's treatment of true negatives is underspecified for open concept spaces.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Strong motivation to pair semantic/lexical scores with source-grounded concept audits, but the ARR project should preregister an open-world matching rubric and disclose coder/sample independence.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: peer-reviewed Qualitative Health Research article, first online 24 December 2025; volume 36 issue 2-3, March 2026, pages 181-190
records.decision_reason: ARC is an evidence-informed conceptual checklist, not a primary LLM coding study; it directly informs oversight and preregistration decisions.

Research objective.value: Provide a pre-analysis reflexivity checkpoint that assigns an appropriate delegate, assist/augment or human-led posture before LLM qualitative coding.
Research objective.anchor: official SAGE full text, Introduction/AI-Reflexivity Checklist

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: evidence-informed conceptual/methodological framework for qualitative health research

Actual operationalized methodology.value: The author synthesizes science-and-technology studies, empirical AI-assisted qualitative-analysis studies and pragmatic workflows into five sequential decision domains; no empirical validation of ARC is conducted.
Actual operationalized methodology.anchor: official SAGE full text, Abstract/AI-Reflexivity Checklist

Generated outputs.value: five prompts/domains: descriptive/intellective scope, contextual variation, experiential depth, ethical exposure and output reversibility; associated HITL posture bands

Human role.value: Researchers document analytic intention and risk before model use, set acceptance criteria, verify delegated work and retain human-led control for experiential/ethical risk or irreversibility.
Human role.anchor: official SAGE full text, ARC checklist

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: A dated posture decision is intended as a brief review record; reversibility is treated as a prerequisite for audit/repair.

Principal results.value: ARC permits bounded automation only when classification is descriptive, meanings stable, nuance and ethical exposure low, and outputs fully reversible; elevated experiential/ethical risk pushes toward assistance or human leadership.
Principal results.anchor: official SAGE full text, ARC decision logic

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Ethical exposure is one of five gating domains; author reports no subjects/ethics-board requirement and discloses MS Copilot/ChatGPT-4o manuscript assistance.
Ethics and privacy treatment.anchor: official SAGE full text, Ethical Considerations/Author's Note

Author-reported limitations.value: Presented as a first draft intended for community revision; empirical reliability, predictive validity and inter-team consistency are not established.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: the five posture decisions depend on subjective ratings without validated thresholds or demonstrated inter-rater reliability; a checklist can document but cannot itself prevent automation bias or path dependence.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Direct basis for a preregistered pre-analysis risk gate and reversibility requirement, with the ARR project able to add empirical scoring reliability and acceptance thresholds.
Relevance to the proposed ARR project.anchor: official SAGE full text, ARC checklist

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: arXiv preprint 2602.19690v1, submitted 23 February 2026; peer review not established
records.decision_reason: The primary LLM task is political-news classification and explanation influence rather than qualitative coding, though the human-AI reliance experiment and thematic analysis of reasons are methodologically adjacent.

Research objective.value: Evaluate GPT political-ideology classification and test how brief versus detailed explanations change crowdworkers' labels, confidence and reasoning.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: systematic thematic analysis of open-ended participant reasons embedded in a mixed quantitative experiment

Actual operationalized methodology.value: GPT-4o/mini prompts are benchmarked on historical 34k and recent 17k news corpora; 124 MTurk participants classify three articles before and after seeing brief or detailed GPT-4o explanations, then two researchers code 372 explanations of agreement/disagreement.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: deductive three-class annotation plus inductive/thematic coding of participant reasons

Domain.value: US political-news ideology and human-AI annotation

Number of documents.value: 34k historical news dataset, 17k recent articles, 60 selected study articles, and 372 open-ended participant responses

Number of participants.value: 124 MTurk participants in two explanation conditions

Exact model/version.value: GPT-4o and GPT-4o mini; dated snapshots not reported

Prompting strategy.value: Several role/definition/source-cue prompts and a self-critique prompt tested; selected prompt A with temperature 0, adding brief or detailed explanation instructions.

Human role.value: Crowdworkers make initial/final labels and reasons; researchers code reasons and interpret reliance; humans can be persuaded by incorrect model explanations.
Human role.anchor: Why do you agree or disagree with AI

Unit of analysis.value: news article for classification and participant open-ended rationale for thematic analysis

Generated outputs.value: left/center/right label, brief or detailed rationale, participant label/confidence changes and themes of agreement/disagreement

Automatic metrics.value: precision, recall, F1, accuracy, MAE, MCC, BERTScore, readability, perplexity, confidence change, switching and agreement

Human-evaluation design.value: Between-subjects brief/detailed explanation experiment; three within-person articles with pre/post label and confidence; two researchers develop/code qualitative reasons, but thematic IRR is not reported.

Principal results.value: GPT-4o recent-data F1 was at most .42/accuracy about .45 in reported configurations. AI explanations increased confidence even when wrong; detailed explanations changed 19.89% of decisions versus 7.53% for brief explanations and sometimes reduced accuracy.
Principal results.anchor: accuracy dropped from an initial 26% to 18%

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Consent is shown in the survey flow; recruitment/payment/IRB and sensitive-data details require fuller reporting than appears in the extracted text.

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors discuss subjective/ambiguous labels, source-based ground truth, MTurk sample/task constraints, limited articles and prompt/model dependence.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: outlet-derived labels are not objective ideology ground truth; low GPT accuracy makes the study primarily an automation-bias warning; the qualitative codebook/IRR are underreported and each participant sees only three articles.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Adjacent evidence that plausible detailed rationales can raise confidence and induce wrong qualitative judgments; explanations require correctness-aware reliance outcomes, not readability alone.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: medRxiv preprint posted 9 July 2026; explicitly not certified by peer review as of cutoff
records.decision_reason: The preprint reports a dual-model, clinician-validated thematic coding workflow with calibration data, multiple agreement estimands, disclosed outputs and clear separation of low- versus high-interpretation layers.

Research objective.value: Describe how patient/caregiver CDI burden changes by recurrence and fulminant severity using scalable, validated LLM-assisted thematic coding.

Claimed qualitative methodology.value: retrospective thematic analysis with a priori domains, emergent semantic fields and narrative arcs

Actual operationalized methodology.value: Claude and DeepSeek independently classify cohorts and code eight domains/four severity flags; Claude proposes recurring expressions that the PI clusters into 13 semantic fields and both models recode corpus; both assign dominant domain/14-category arc; synthetic held-out calibration and blinded clinician coding quantify reliability, with PI adjudication.

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: hybrid: a priori clinical domains/flags plus model-proposed, PI-clustered emergent semantic fields

Number of documents.value: 204 public testimonials retrieved; 15 unclassifiable exclusions; 189 analysed across rfCDI 49, fCDI 18, rCDI 84 and non-rfCDI 38

Number of participants.value: 189 testimonial authors/narratives (30 caregiver-authored; unique-person status not verified); two senior internal-medicine resident raters and one PI adjudicator

Sensitive-data status.value: public illness narratives with reidentification risk; identifying details/underlying text not redistributed and quotations limited to nonidentifying excerpts

Exact model/version.value: Claude Sonnet 4.6 and DeepSeek V4 Pro, temperature 0; exact API snapshots not reported
Exact model/version.anchor: Both models were queried at temperature zero

Prompting strategy.value: Structured binary and single-choice coding prompts calibrated on 60 synthetic literature-grounded cases; explicit thresholds added for adjacent domains; held-out validation; final prompt deployed unchanged and openly shared.

Human role.value: Investigators define criteria, PI adjudicates 34 cohort and 28 coding disagreements, clusters emergent expressions, and interprets findings; two blinded clinicians independently code reliability sample.

Unit of analysis.value: complete testimonial with binary domain/flag/semantic-field labels, one dominant domain and one narrative arc

Generated outputs.value: cohort labels, 8 domains, 4 flags, 13 semantic fields, dominant dimension, 14-category arc, per-testimonial dual-model labels and cohort frequencies

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: Deidentified row-level dual-model outputs, prompts, calibration corpus, dictionary and analysis code are archived; source narratives available from foundation rather than redistributed.

Number of runs or seeds.value: one zero-temperature coding run per model; model-model agreement used as reproducibility evidence, but repeated same-model runs not reported

Automatic metrics.value: macro F1 on synthetic calibration; PABAK primary, Gwet AC1 convergent, conditional Cohen kappa, percent agreement and descriptive cohort frequencies

Human-evaluation design.value: Two residents blinded to each other/models code 16 edge-spanning testimonials, then after calibration independently recode seven; PI-adjudicated 28 disagreements create a reference; human-human, human-Claude and model-model comparisons are reported.

Principal results.value: Human-human PABAK .788 for semantic fields and .757 for binary domains/flags; human-LLM semantic-field PABAK .596-.731. Arc agreement was weakest (human-human 68.8%; human-LLM 37.5%-43.8%). Models systematically undercalled implied psychosocial fields and overcalled diagnostic failure relative to clinicians.

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: Authors determine public testimonials are not human-subjects research; no identifiers, limited excerpts, nonredistribution of underlying narratives and deidentified outputs; model data-retention terms not reported.

Author-reported limitations.value: Descriptive/no inference; self-selected severe single-platform sample; patient-reported unverified clinical details; nonclinical recurrence definition; model-behavior contamination and low arc reliability; human-LLM divergence on implied psychosocial content.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: n=16 human validation (only seven post-calibration) is too small for stable per-code estimates; PI-generated semantic grouping and adjudicated reference are not independent; averaging two models can conceal systematic directional error, and synthetic calibration may not represent narrative ambiguity.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: A high-value design for layered construct difficulty, prevalence-aware agreement and open row-level artifacts; its tiny human sample and systematic psychosocial underdetection motivate larger blinded expert evaluation.

records.publication_status_as_of_cutoff: PsyArXiv/OSF preprint, second draft, 2026; peer review not established
records.decision_reason: ROCK 1.0 is a qualitative-data interoperability/provenance standard rather than an LLM evaluation, but it supplies directly relevant source identifiers, codebook and workflow structures.

Research objective.value: Specify a plain-text human- and machine-readable standard for interoperable, FAIR coded qualitative data and codebooks.

Claimed qualitative methodology.anchor: standard for human- and machine-readable qualitative

Actual operationalized methodology.value: The paper normatively specifies ROCK 1.0 syntax and project topology for source utterances, IDs, character spans, codes/relationships/values, segmentation, nesting, metadata, anchors, notes, YAML/spreadsheet codebooks and executable workflows, with worked examples.
Actual operationalized methodology.anchor: The elements of the ROCK standard

Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.value: method-neutral; supports inductive and deductive codebooks
Inductive, deductive, or hybrid.anchor: either a predefined deductive codebook, or an inductively produced codebook

Domain.value: general qualitative data and open science

Human role.value: Researchers segment sources, define/apply codes, document positionality/process and choose what sensitive data can be shared; software parses and merges explicit structures.

Unit of analysis.value: line/utterance or character span in a plain-text source, identified by UID/TSSID/project reference

Generated outputs.value: .rock sources, YAML/spreadsheet codebooks, metadata/aesthetics/attributes, ROCK project archives and machine-readable workflow graphs

Evidence/provenance mechanism.value: UIDs, timestamped source IDs, shortDOI links, code spans, codebook URCIDs/UCRs, version/author/ORCID/positionality metadata and pipeline stages enable source-level provenance and merging.

Human-evaluation design.value: none reported; examples demonstrate syntax, not user or interoperability testing

Ethics and privacy treatment.value: FAIR/open sharing is emphasized; the standard can encode provenance/attributes but does not itself enforce deidentification, consent, access control or differential sharing.

Author-reported limitations.value: Authors acknowledge the standard is intentionally rudimentary and some relations/features/implementations remain limited or under development.

Additional validity concerns.value: Reviewer concern: a representational standard does not guarantee reliable coding, privacy-safe release, adoption, parser conformance or long-term identifier resolution; empirical interoperability and threat-model tests are absent.

Relevance to the proposed ARR project.value: Concrete schema candidate for source-span traceability, coder/run merges, codebook versioning, positionality and machine-auditable workflow lineage.
